simple.meaning: אִלֵּם (ʼillêm) is a Hebrew word meaning “speechless.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: אִלֵּם (H483) appears 6 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Exodus 4:11, with occurrences in Exodus, Psalms, Proverbs, Isaiah, Habakkuk.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אִלֵּם (H483) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in אִלֵּם (H483) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: אִלֵּם (ʼillêm) / H483 is traced through Exodus 4:11, Psalms 38:14, Proverbs 31:8, Isaiah 35:6 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Yahweh said to him, “Who made man’s mouth? Or who makes one mute, or deaf, or seeing, or blind? Isn’t it I, Yahweh?

timeline.evidenceText: Yahweh said to him, “Who made man’s mouth? Or who makes one mute, or deaf, or seeing, or blind? Isn’t it I, Yahweh?
Yes, I am as a man who doesn’t hear,
Open your mouth for the mute,
Then the lame man will leap like a deer,
“What value does the engraved image have, that its maker has engraved it; the molten image, even the teacher of lies, that he who fashions its form trusts in it, to make mute idols?
